seasonMovement: Impossible arrival -> settlement -> orientation and territory -> navigation -> neighborhood recognition -> participation -> information and self-directed civic use -> provision and provider pressure -> usefulness -> lived belonging without mediation -> chosen household with different wants -> self-defined belonging under judgment.
seasonDramaticShift: Issues 1–8 are driven largely by collision with 2026 and the work of building an ordinary life. From Issue 9 forward, modern systems remain real pressure but stop being the default dramatic protagonist. Trial of Toil, Belonging, War Council and the finale are driven by usefulness, autonomy, chosen routines, different wants, responsibility and legal self-definition.

finaleState.ordeal: Issue 12 residency hearing functions as Bjorn's trial by combat through a genuine record defect: the emergency file still encodes him as the responsible adult for four other adults, and permanent status cannot issue individually until that hierarchy is tested and corrected.
finaleState.hearingPurpose: The institution must decide whether the emergency household classification still describes reality. The hearing can grant five individual permanent statuses only if the applicants establish separate adult agency and the old Bjorn-centered record is lawfully corrected.
finaleState.bjorn: Bjorn arrives in armor without weapons. His decisive act is not a speech: when the Hearing Officer explains that correcting the record removes his formal authority to answer for the others, he says, 'Then correct it.'
finaleState.carrie: Carrie admits she selected Bjorn as responsible adult during emergency intake because the system required one and he could answer enough questions. She earns the result by acknowledging that the designation became inaccurate and supporting five separate permanent findings.
finaleState.astrid: Astrid's independence is proven compactly through self-advocacy, navigation, errands, neighborhood relationships, and the distinction between mutual reliance and legal dependency. Belonging established that she has a life Carrie does not manage; the hearing reveals enough of that life to cure the legal record.

dialogueGuidance.status: guidance only — not a rule, quota, or minimum line count
dialogueGuidance.principle: Include more scenes in each issue where characters remain on one subject long enough to have an actual conversation: questions produce follow-up questions, explanations are tested, people clarify or revise what they mean, and a third person can complicate the exchange. Preserve terse beats when brevity is the point.
productionUse: Do not pad action, reveal, reaction, transition, or punchline pages merely to increase dialogue.

When a social, domestic, procedural, philosophical, or cultural scene wants to linger, allow multiple short turns across the page rather than compressing the idea into question / answer / joke / exit.
Dialogue volume should vary by scene. A sustained conversation may carry many short balloons if the panel plan and lettering remain readable.

Carrie / Bjorn / Gunnar conversations are especially useful when Bjorn tests responsibility or principle, Gunnar follows the system's logic, and Carrie explains or defends how the modern mechanism actually operates.

Astrid, the Kin, recurring neighbors, workers, merchants and officials should also receive ordinary conversational turns when the relationship benefits; fuller dialogue is not reserved for the three leads.
